arxiv-2208-05921.title: A Systematic Study of the Short-Term X-ray Variability of Seyfert Galaxies I. Diversity of the X-ray Rms Spectra
arxiv-2208-05921.creator: Jingwei Hu, Chichuan Jin, Huaqing Cheng, Weimin Yuan
arxiv-2208-05921.description: Abstract The X-ray variability of active galactic nuclei (AGN) carries crucial information about the X-ray radiation mechanism. We performed a systematic study of the X-ray short-term (1–100 ks timescale) variability for a large sample of 78 Seyferts with 426 deep XMM-Newton observations.

arxiv-2210-01768.title: Disentanglement with Biological Constraints: A Theory of Functional Cell Types
arxiv-2210-01768.creator: James C.R. Whittington, William Dorrell, Surya Ganguli, Timothy E.J. Behrens
arxiv-2210-01768.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by James C.R. Whittington, William Dorrell, Surya Ganguli, Timothy E.J. Behrens. Neurons in the brain are often finely tuned for specific task variables. Moreover, such disentangled representations are highly sought after in machine learning. Here we mathematically prove that simple biological constraints on neurons, namely nonnegativity and energy efficiency in both activity and weights, promote such sought after disentangled representations by enforcing neurons to become selective for single factors of task variation.

arxiv-2302-01805.title: Model-free inequality for data of Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen-Bohm experiments
arxiv-2302-01805.creator: Hans De Raedt, Mikhail I. Katsnelson, Manpreet S. Jattana, Vrinda Mehta, Madita Willsch, Dennis Willsch, Kristel Michielsen, Fengping Jin
arxiv-2302-01805.description: Abstract We present a new inequality constraining correlations obtained when performing Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen-Bohm experiments. The proof does not rely on mathematical models that are imagined to have produced the data and is therefore “model-free”. The new inequality contains the model-free version of the well-known Bell-CHSH inequality as a special case.

arxiv-2309-00629.title: Quantifying MEV on L2s: A Study of Polygon, Arbitrum, and Optimism
arxiv-2309-00629.creator: Arthur Bagourd & Luca Georges Francois
arxiv-2309-00629.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Arthur Bagourd & Luca Georges Francois. This work was financed by a research grant from Flashbots [ 1 ] . Abstract : This paper addresses the lack of research on quantifying Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) on Ethereum Layer 2 networks (L2s). Our findings reveal a substantial amount of MEV to be extracted on L2s, particularly on Polygon, with a lower bound of $213 million surpassing previous estimates.

arxiv-2310-09637.title: Asymptotic symmetries of gravity in the gauge PDE approach
arxiv-2310-09637.creator: Maxim Grigoriev a,b and Mikhail Markov a,b,c
arxiv-2310-09637.description: Abstract We propose a framework to study local gauge theories on manifolds with boundaries and asymptotic symmetries, which is based on representing them as so-called gauge PDEs. These objects extend the conventional BV-AKSZ sigma-models to the case of not necessarily topological and diffeomorphism invariant systems and are known to behave well with respect to restrictions to submanifolds and boundaries.

arxiv-2404-09084.title: Noncommutative weighted shifts, joint similarity, and function theory in several variables
arxiv-2404-09084.creator: Gelu Popescu
arxiv-2404-09084.description: Abstract . The goal of this paper is to study the structure of noncommutative weighted shifts, their properties, and to understand their role as models (up to similarity) for n n -tuples of operators on Hilbert spaces as well as their implications to function theory on noncommutative (resp.commutative) Reinhardt domains.

arxiv-2405-19079.title: On the Influence of Smoothness Constraints in Computed Tomography Motion Compensation
arxiv-2405-19079.creator: Mareike Thies, Fabian Wagner, Noah Maul, Siyuan Mei, Mingxuan Gu, Laura Pfaff, Nastassia Vysotskaya, Haijun Yu, and Andreas Maier
arxiv-2405-19079.description: Abstract Computed tomography (CT) relies on precise patient immobilization during image acquisition. Nevertheless, motion artifacts in the reconstructed images can persist. Motion compensation methods aim to correct such artifacts post-acquisition, often incorporating temporal smoothness constraints on the estimated motion patterns.

arxiv-2408-11445.title: Verifying Approximate Equilibrium in Auctions
arxiv-2408-11445.creator: Fabian R. Pieroth, Tuomas Sandholm
arxiv-2408-11445.description: Abstract In practice, most auction mechanisms are not strategy-proof, so equilibrium analysis is required to predict bidding behavior. In many auctions, though, an exact equilibrium is not known and one would like to understand whether—manually or computationally generated—bidding strategies constitute an approximate equilibrium.

arxiv-2508-15233.title: Pretrained Diffusion Models Are Inherently Skipped-Step Samplers
arxiv-2508-15233.creator: Wenju Xu xuwenju123@gmail.com
arxiv-2508-15233.description: Abstract Diffusion models have been achieving state-of-the-art results across various generation tasks. However, a notable drawback is their sequential generation process, requiring long-sequence step-by-step generation. Existing methods, such as DDIM, attempt to reduce sampling steps by constructing a class of non-Markovian diffusion processes that maintain the same training objective.

pmc-13072926.title: Revealing GRK5 Activation Features by Interpretable Machine Learning and Molecular Dynamics Simulation
pmc-13072926.creator: Yuanpeng Song, Ming Kong, Fuhui Zhang, Xuemei Pu
pmc-13072926.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). G protein-coupled receptor kinase 5 (GRK5) is an important therapeutic target involving cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and inflammatory disorders. However, the features of its activation as an essential function regulation process have been poorly understood, limiting related drug development. The work utilizes a molecular dynamics simulation coupled with an interpretable machine learning model to identify key structure and dynamics determinants distinguishing the active and inactive states of GRK5.

pmc-13366382.creator: Unknown
pmc-13366382.description: Between January and May 2026, 109 confirmed cases of Salmonella Bovismorbificans ST377 were reported from 10 European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA) countries (Austria, Belgium, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, Spain and the Netherlands) and the United Kingdom. The outbreak predominantly affected adult females. Eighteen cases required hospitalisation. Two deaths were reported in Finland (one confirmed and one probable case).

pmc-13372170.title: Spatial inequalities in breastfeeding initiation in the United States: A multiscale analysis of county-level determinants
pmc-13372170.creator: Tony H. Grubesic, Wei Kang, Kelly M. Durbin, Edward Helderop
pmc-13372170.description: Deepening our understanding of geographic variations in breastfeeding initiation (BFI) remains an important element in developing a comprehensive snapshot of maternal and infant health. Identifying spatial variations in socioeconomic, demographic, cultural, and environmental barriers to breastfeeding can advance intervention efforts to educate and encourage breastfeeding within a community.

pmc-13387202.title: Factors Influencing Psychological Help-Seeking Intention for Women with Perinatal Depression and Their Spouses: A Scoping Review
pmc-13387202.creator: Qinhan Zou, Yanli Mao, Siying Zhang, Ying Zhuang, Xianliang Liu, Xia Duan
pmc-13387202.description: BackgroundProfessional psychological help can significantly improve outcomes for women with perinatal depression (PND), yet many delay or avoid seeking it. Spouses significantly influence women’s help-seeking decisions. However, comprehensive reviews synthesizing factors affecting both women’s and their spouses’ intentions, particularly regarding spousal support, remain lacking.

pmc-13445414.title: Automatic coarse-to-fine AC-PC localization on CT using registration-guided 3D-UNets
pmc-13445414.creator: Sharada Kadaba Sridhar, Alyssa Eastman, Peter Wilson, Shubhendu Mishra, Charles Broadbent, Chip Truwit, Rui Kuang, Uzma Samadani
pmc-13445414.description: IntroductionAutomatically localizing the Anterior Commissure (AC) and Posterior Commissure (PC) is foundational for CT-based algorithmic disease screening, yet robust computational methods for this on CT remain lacking. We developed a registration-guided 3D-UNet framework for CT-based AC-PC localization, demonstrating its utility in computing ventriculomegaly features for Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH) detection.
